license: Original source: Weiss et al. (2025), CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Numerical facts transcribed with attribution; no source figures or article text redistributed. Interpretation notes are project-authored.
coverage: All 15 entries in SI Table S1, plus the separately studied NWA 7034 contamination suite. Not all known Martian meteorites and not all published experiments. The review mentions approximately 18 studied pairing groups, a different scope.
uncertainty_note: Reported paleointensity errors have mixed definitions, omit important calibration systematics in many non-thermal studies, and must not be used as comparable Gaussian 1σ errors. Null means unreported, never zero. Bounds remain bounds. No pooled mean, dynamo duration or hemispheric fit is calculated.
transcription_notes: The caption repeats depleted for S-int; we expand S-int as intermediate and retain the original labels in the source PDF.
ALH 84001 uncertainty is 75 Ma; the superscript 2 is a footnote, not a digit.
MIL chronology in this synthesis differs from other published ages; no silent harmonization was applied.

records.name: Tissint
records.age_convention: 95% interval in compilation; generally a crystallization-age proxy, potentially an upper bound on remanence acquisition
records.reading_depth: Primary paper: paleomagnetic results and discussion consulted
records.interpretation: Gattacceca et al. interpret the surviving record as partial thermoremanence acquired during cooling after shock, before ejection. It is secondary relative to igneous crystallization but still a Martian signal. The roughly 2.3 µT estimate is not evidence that a dynamo was operating at the crystallization age.

events.constraint: Younger than crystallization; distinct from ejection in the paper interpretation

records.name: MIL 03346
records.age_convention: 95% interval in compilation; generally a crystallization-age proxy, potentially an upper bound on remanence acquisition
records.reading_depth: Primary paper: methods, results and discussion consulted; bulk laboratory files acquired
records.interpretation: Interior high-coercivity directions and a fusion-crust contact test support pre-terrestrial remanence. The authors favour thermal acquisition during emplacement; high-temperature thermochemical contributions are considered. Low-coercivity components are terrestrial overprints. A local crustal field can explain the reported paleointensity without a late dynamo.
records.pairing_note: Pairs mentioned by Volk et al.; the downloaded experiment is MIL 03346, not measurements of all four stones.

records.name: ALH 84001
records.age_convention: Oldest inferred recording event only; 95% interval in synthesis
records.reading_depth: Primary paper: methods and interpretation consulted; MagIC archive acquired
records.interpretation: Mineral-scale records are interpreted as multiple ancient components, potentially involving reversals and impact heating. The table age denotes only the oldest inferred recording event, not every component. Laboratory directions do not locate the meteorite on Mars. The archived QDM moments are fitted magnetic sources, not whole-rock moments.

records.name: NWA 7034 paired stones
records.age_convention: Clast formation, breccia assembly and remagnetization are distinct events.
records.reading_depth: Primary contamination study consulted; MagIC measurements acquired
records.interpretation: Nine examined paired stones were remagnetized by hand magnets on Earth. Their curves document contamination, not an ancient Martian field. Geochemistry and petrography remain useful; this result must not be generalized to every untested specimen.
